'''María Heloísa Juana Rojas Corradi''' (born 10 August 1972), known as '''Maisa Rojas''' is a [[Chilean people|Chilean]] [[politician]], [[physicist]], and [[climatologist]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://elpais.com/sociedad/2019/09/24/actualidad/1569356630_151425.html|title='Nuestras estimaciones sobre los riesgos del cambio climático fueron muy conservadoras'|work=El País |publisher=[[El País]]|date=25 September 2021|accessdate=11 March 2022 |last1=Planelles |first1=Manuel }}</ref> who has been serving as [[Ministry for the Environment (Chile)|Minister for the Environment]] since 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.latercera.com/politica/noticia/quien-es-maisa-rojas-la-nueva-ministra-de-medio-ambiente-de-gabriel-boric/WABEL2PBEFA2ZPTZYFDFKAU6PY/|title=Quién es Maisa Rojas, la nueva ministra de Medio Ambiente de Gabriel Boric|publisher=[[La Tercera]]|date=21 January 2022|accessdate=13 March 2022}}</ref>

==Early life and education==

Rojas received her undergraduate degree in physics from the [[University of Chile]] and her Ph.D. in atmospheric physics from [[Lincoln College, Oxford]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maisa Rojas |url=https://www.wilsoncenter.org/person/maisa-rojas |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200726054536/https://www.wilsoncenter.org/person/maisa-rojas |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 26, 2020 |access-date=2022-03-20 |website=www.wilsoncenter.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-02-05 |title='We need politicians and experts': how Chile is putting the climate crisis first |url=https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/feb/05/we-need-politicians-and-experts-maisa-rojas-how-chile-putting-climate-crisis-first |access-date=2022-03-20 |website=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref>

==Career==

===Career in academia===
Rojas was a postdoctoral fellow at the [[International Research Institute for Climate and Society]] at [[Columbia University]] in 2001.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Women who Inspire: Maisa Rojas {{!}} Columbia Global Centers |url=https://globalcenters.columbia.edu/news/women-who-inspire-maisa-rojas |access-date=2022-03-20 |website=globalcenters.columbia.edu}}</ref> She then returned to the Universidad de Chile as a postdoctoral fellow, researcher, and later as a professor of [[geophysics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Maisa Rojas |url=http://dgf.uchile.cl/~maisa/Maisa_english/Maisa_Rojas.html |access-date=2022-03-20 |website=dgf.uchile.cl |archive-date=2023-04-12 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230412114501/http://dgf.uchile.cl/~maisa/Maisa_english/Maisa_Rojas.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

During that time, Rojas became an internationally leading climate change scientist. She was the lead author of the Paleoclimate chapter for the UN Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change's (IPCC) fifth report (AR5) and was also a coordinating lead author for the IPCC report (AR6). She has served on various presidential councils and committees on climate change.<ref name=":0" />

===Career in government===
In 2022, Chilean President [[Gabriel Boric]] named Rojas Minister for the Environment in his cabinet.<ref>Natalia A. Ramos Miranda and Fabian Cambero (21 January 2022), [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-chile-politics-idAFKBN2JV27M 'Something has changed': young, female-led Cabinet reflects Chile's modern twist] ''[[Reuters]]''.</ref>

Rojas, along with [[Jennifer Morgan (activist)|Jennifer Morgan]], led the working group at the [[2022 United Nations Climate Change Conference]] that developed an agreement on [[loss and damage (climate change)|loss and damage]] finance.<ref>[https://unfccc.int/sites/default/files/resource/16%20November%20COP27%20President%20update.pdf Letter to Parties and Observers, 16 November 2022] [[United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change]].</ref><ref>Jake Spring and Valerie Volcovici (7 December 2022), [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/after-un-climate-deal-loss-damage-funding-two-years-off-2022-12-07/ After U.N. climate deal, 'loss and damage' funding two years off] ''[[Reuters]]''.</ref>

In a mid-2023 interview, following one year as environment minister, Rojas stated that a major reason for entering politics was to prevent noted climate denier [[José Antonio Kast]] from becoming president. Rojas also does not believe that present government institutions are equipped to deal with the scale of the [[Climate crisis|climate emergency]] we face. Nonetheless, Rojas believes that a [[just transition]] to [[Carbon neutrality|net-zero]] is a{{nbsp}}necessity.<ref name="watts-2023">{{cite news | last1 = Watts | first1 = Jonathan | title = Climate scientist Maisa Rojas: 'I have a mandate to be part of Chile's first ecological, feminist government' | date = 8 July 2023 | work = The Guardian | location = London, United Kingdom | issn = 0029-7712 | url = https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2023/jul/08/climate-scientist-politician-maisa-rojas-chile-government-climate | access-date = 2023-07-09 }}</ref>
